# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (compact reference)

## BOOK 1 — The Layton Court Mystery (Anthony Berkeley, Gutenberg 72883)

**Characters**
- Roger Sheringham: amateur sleuth/author, <40, stocky, round face, gray eyes, Norfolk jacket, big-bowled pipe, Winchester & Oxford, half-blue golf. Calls unmarried ladies under 30 by first names. Narrator-style "Holmes" foil; Alec is "Watson."
- Alexander "Alec" Grierson: big, broad-shouldered, cheerful, Oxford cricketer (3 yrs), Scots ("Scotch"), young (≈24 implied), engaged to Barbara Shannon on day 1; later broke it off.
- Victor Stanworth: host, ~60, genial, rich City man, bachelor, found dead in library, shot in centre of forehead; revolver in right hand; typed "suicide" note with "V-i-c" false start. Blackmailer.
- Lady Cynthia Stanworth (Lady Stanworth): hostess, Victor's sister-in-law (widow of younger brother), tall, graying, dignified; secretly married to Major Jefferson; was blackmailed by Victor over her father the Earl of Grassingham.
- Major Jefferson (Harry): secretary, tall, sallow, taciturn, ex-army; was blackmailed over forged check; secretly married to Lady Stanworth ~6 months earlier.
- Graves (real name Bill Higgins): butler, ex-prize-fighter, huge; hated Stanworth.
- Barbara Shannon: 19, fair, grey-eyed; daughter of Mrs. Shannon; broke engagement to Alec on day 1; was blackmailed by Victor about her mother's past.
- Mrs. Shannon: small, fair, doll-like, peevish.
- Mary Plant (Mrs. Plant): ~26, dark-haired, husband in Soudanese Civil Service; blackmailed by Victor over pre-marriage incident; jewels pretext; crying in library; jasmine scent (Parfum Jasmine).
- Inspector Mansfield (Elchester police); Dr. Matthewson (doctor); Rudgeman (constable); William (gardener, greenfly); Mrs. William (lodge, cook's brother story); Chapman (chauffeur); Albert (landlord of village inn); Halbert (showfure/groom); Alice, Mary (maids); Mr. Wetherby (Hillcrest Farm); John Prince (suspect, bull incident); Anna.
- Maurice/"Lady Stanworth" etc.; Mrs. Plant's husband unnamed.

**Events in order**
1. Morning 8am, Layton Court rose garden. William gardener despondent over greenfly. Roger meets Alec; Alec admits he was posting a letter to bookmaker in village. Alec then meets Barbara who says she cannot marry him (engagement of previous day cancelled, "something dreadful happened").
2. Breakfast: Victor's background; party guests; Major Jefferson summoned by Graves. Lady Stanworth announces Victor's bedroom unslept, library locked inside. Major Jefferson, Graves, Alec, Roger break library door. Victor dead: shot himself (apparent). Typed statement "For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself."
3. Roger notices the wound is in centre of forehead (unnatural). Dr. Matthewson estimates death ~2am. Inspector Mansfield arrives; examines safe; safe's keys in wrong waistcoat pocket; combination unknown. Jefferson searching pockets; alarm about safe.
4. Interviews: last seen by Mrs. Plant (in hall ~10pm). Roger and Victor smoked in garden ~10pm. Mrs. Plant claims she went to library to retrieve jewels from safe — lie revealed later.
5. Roger & Alec: Roger suspects murder; four curious people (Graves, Lady Stanworth, Jefferson, Mrs. Plant). Pen/ vase: a blue vase broken by bullet; bullet mark in chimney-piece panel; second shot fired from Victor's revolver (only one empty shell found). Blotter shows fountain-pen scratches; crumpled signed sheet in waste basket → confession faked.
6. Barbara tells Alec "it was a horrible coincidence"; asks him to wait till next month.
7. Roger's theories; footprint at lattice window; ash pit; scrap of paper "that brute Prince"; William's wife warns about John Prince (attacked Stanworth earlier); bull chase at Hillcrest Farm; station & village inquiries; William saw large man at 8:30pm (cook's "brother").
8. Woman's handkerchief (jasmine) and face powder on settee; hair found → woman in library. Mary says settee tidied; Roger confronts Mrs. Plant; she admits she was in library with Stanworth (blackmail); Victor's letter claims he burnt evidence.
9. Jefferson confesses to Roger (blackmail over forgery in India; Lady Stanworth & Jefferson married secretly). Jefferson alibi: with wife.
10. Discovery: Alec was the killer. Alec went to library in pyjamas ~ midnight; witnessed Victor blackmailing Mrs. Plant; then Barbara (blackmailed about her mother; Mrs. Shannon's past). Alec confronted Victor; Victor fired and missed (hit vase); Alec forced revolver to Victor's forehead and fired. Alec burnt blackmail documents, faked suicide (typed note, extracted cartridge, locked windows with lattice-handle trick, footprints). Alec exited window; re-entered via dining room.

**Ending**: Inquest verdict "Suicide during temporary insanity." Roger & Alec take train to London; Alec's confession; Roger: "try not to be so disgustingly conventional."

**Notable quotes/details**: Inspector: "It's not my job to know anything..." Roger's Holmes/Watson patter; Mrs. Plant's jasmine "Parfum Jasmine, nine and sixpence." Barbara's mother = Mrs. Shannon. Lady Stanworth's earl: Earl of Grassingham.

## BOOK 2 — Linda Carlton, Air Pilot (Edith Lavell, Gutenberg 44862)

**Characters**
- Linda Carlton: 17→18, blue eyes, fair/golden hair, small slight, Spring City graduate (Miss Graham's school); voted most popular girl; dreams of flying; sports roadster (her father's gift at 16); Pursuit (Arrow Sport biplane) gift.
- Tom Carlton (Father): tall, lithe, dark hair graying temples, ranch in Texas, absent-minded, stern; hated Mackay's father (Mr. Mackay, who stole on his ranch).
- Aunt Emily Carlton (Miss Carlton): father's sister, raised Linda after mother died; disapproves of planes; wants social life.
- Ted (Edward) Mackay: big, red hair, blue eyes, flyer; mother a fine woman; older sister; father a thief; sent Linda 3 May-class flowers; instructor/flyer at Spring City Flying School; later sales pilot for Kansas City firm.
- Ralph Clavering: wealthy, Harvard; father millionaire oil man; sister Kitty Clavering (pearl necklace, $50,000, insured).
- Louise (Lou) Haydock: best friend; dark sleek short hair, earrings; mother Mrs. Haydock.
- Maurice Stetson (Maurry): "prince of wise-crackers", Ralph's Harvard roommate, crashed plane earlier.
- Harriman "Harry" Smith: engineering student, nice; partner for ball; later Louise's interest.
- Dot Crowley (tiny blonde), Jim Valier (tall thin), Sara Wheeler, Sue Emery, Jackson Stiles, Joe Sinclair.
- Lieutenant Kingsberry (school head, ex-Army); H.B. Taylor (instructor, condescending); the "Waco" flyer = thief (unlicensed man, the school's errand boy).
- Mr. Jordan (sales manager, Kansas City); Sam Hunter (Ted's company pilot).
- Mrs. Stillman (Aunt Margaret), Sunny Hills, Colorado; children Roger (31), Anita, twins Dan & David, Jennie, Elsie.
- Mrs. Cates (ranch housekeeper), Dr. Winston, Dr. Lineaweaver (St. Louis surgeon, vacation in Louisiana), Cates (ranch hand).
- German shack man ("Nicht versteh").

**Events in order**
1. Ch 1: Linda's first flight with Ted Mackay in old biplane; engine fails; both parachute; Linda calm. Ted lands safely.
2. Ch 2: Class-day/graduation at Miss Graham's school. Linda gets bracelet "most popular." Prophecy: Linda & Louise will marry rich men. Linda's aunt; flowers (pink roses from Ted, no card). Father absent for graduation.
3. Ch 3: Picnic (Grier's woods); swimming; treasure hunt; Linda's father arrives; gift = Arrow Sport biplane "Pursuit" and hangar. Father agrees she can take commercial course; compromise: summer at home, go to Green Falls August.
4. Ch 4: Father says Ted's father is untrustworthy; forbids friendship. Ralph Clavering decides to enroll at flying school too. Night shows the "Pursuit"; stranger (Ted) spotted on hill; boys chase.
5. Ch 5: First lesson: H.B. Taylor condescends; Lt. Kingsberry; Linda's father forbids Ted; Linda assigned Taylor. Linda's father drives her roadster home; Ted waves at her.
6. Ch 6: License obtained; stunts (inside loops, Immelman); Linda and Ted farewell (Ted leaving for Kansas City). Ralph reveals Midsummer Ball at Green Falls July 31; Kitty's pearls to be carried.
7. Ch 7: Aunt buys flying suit (white knickers, blue sweater, helmet). Flight to Green Falls with Ralph carrying pearl necklace. Lost box near field; thief (unlicensed Waco pilot) returns it for $20 tip.
8. Ch 8: Arrival at Green Falls; box discovered empty; theft realized. Linda & Ralph fly searching; Ralph flies. Landing at wreck of the Waco; Linda sees Ted Mackay unconscious in ambulance.
9. Ch 9: Linda faints; Ralph suspicious; Mr. Carlton & Clavering talk; Mr. Clavering insurance not covering air travel.
10. Ch 10: Ted in hospital (shot by thief, plane stolen); Carlton & Ralph visit, accuse him; Ted screams; nurse orders them out.
11. Ch 11: Linda's father at home, says Ted guilty. Parachute jump disclosed (with Lt. Kingsberry). Canoe party; Linda plans call to hospital.
12. Ch 12: Nurse says Ted went home; Linda searches for thief by air; Ralph reports gas-station evidence; quarrel; Louise arranges Harriman Smith as Linda's partner for ball.
13. Ch 13: Masque ball; Linda as fairy queen (costume chosen by aunt); prize for most beautiful; Ralph and Louise win dance prize.
14. Ch 14: Louise and Linda plan trip; Linda goes to Kansas City to establish Ted's alibi via Mr. Jordan; written statement. Louise accompanies.
15. Ch 15: Sunny Hills (Stillman estate, Colorado). Father telegram: "Your father seriously hurt. Fly to ranch at once." Roger gives map.
16. Ch 16: Flight to Texas; engine trouble (Dan had flown Pursuit at night); forced landing in brush country; lunch; supper; stranded.
17. Ch 17: They find necklace in wrecked plane's coat by stream; two dead men (thieves, one red-haired = Ted's father); night camp.
18. Ch 18: Ted's company (Sam Hunter) secures alibi; Ted's mother; Ted arrives at Stillman's; Roger buys Ted's plane; search; German shack man reveals girls alive.
19. Ch 19: Roger & Ted rescue; Linda to ranch; Mrs. Cates; father unconscious; doctor says operation only chance; Linda flies night to St. Louis/Louisiana.
20. Ch 20: Ted's father was one of the dead thieves; Linda flies to Dr. Lineaweaver (Louisiana seaport), returns at dawn; operation success.
21. Ch 21: Father recovering; Aunt Emily arrives; Field Day at Green Falls; Linda wins airplane race; awarded medal for saving life; father approves of Ted as friend.

**Notes**: Pursuit = Arrow Sport; Waco = school's plane; Linda's father's ranch in Texas; ranch name not given; Linda's roadster; Ted's mother "fine woman"; key motifs: height safety, parachute.
